etymologies.heading: Etymology 1
paragraphs: From Middle English quaylen, from Middle Dutch queilen, quēlen, from Old Dutch *quelan, from Proto-West Germanic *kwelan, from Proto-Germanic *kwelaną (“to suffer”). Doublet of queal.
senses: (intransitive) To waste away; to fade, to wither. [from 15th c.]
(transitive, now rare) To daunt or frighten (someone). [from 16th c.]

etymologies.heading: Etymology 2
paragraphs: From Middle English quayle, quaile, quaille, from Anglo-Norman quaille, from Late Latin quaccola (“quail”).
(prostitute): So called because the quail was thought to be a very amorous bird.
senses: Any of various small game birds of the genera Coturnix, Anurophasis or Perdicula in the Old World family Phasianidae or of the New World family Odontophoridae.
